title: Interpretable Humans, Alien LLMs: Expert Analysis of Latent Structures in Assessment Responses
abstract: arXiv:2608.17810v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The evaluation of large language models (LLMs) relies heavily on human-designed assessments, implicitly assuming that AI and humans employ similar underlying cognitive constructs. Challenging this assumption, we investigate whether the latent factors governing LLM performance carry the same substantive, human-interpretable meaning as the cognitive constructs governing human learners. Using responses from humans and six LLMs across quantitative reasoning and chemistry assessments, we conducted Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) separately for both groups. Subject-Matter Experts (SMEs) then blindly evaluated the resulting factor graphs to ascribe pedagogical meaning to the emerged constructs. SMEs successfully interpreted most of the human-derived factors. translated_title: 可解释的人类，异类的LLM：评估响应中潜在结构的专家分析
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17810v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）的评估在很大程度上依赖于人类设计的评估，这隐含地假设了AI和人类使用相似的底层认知结构。为挑战这一假设，我们研究了控制LLM性能的潜在因素是否具有与人类学习者认知结构相同的实质性、人类可解释的意义。我们使用定量推理和化学评估中人类和六个LLM的响应数据，分别对两组进行了探索性因素分析（EFA）。领域专家（SMEs）随后盲目评估所得的因素图，以赋予这些涌现结构以教学意义。SMEs成功解释了大多数人类衍生的因素。相反，他们无法为定量推理中任何LLM衍生的因素赋予意义，且仅能解释化学中一半的LLM因素。通过结合数据驱动的EFA与专家判断，我们的研究揭示了LLM和人类在认知结构上的显著差异，表明依赖人类为中心的评估可能无法完全捕捉LLM的能力。
tldr: 本文通过探索性因素分析和专家评估，发现LLM在评估中的潜在认知结构与人类显著不同，人类专家难以解释LLM衍生因素，挑战了AI评估中人类认知结构普遍性的假设。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through exploratory factor analysis and expert evaluation that LLMs exhibit latent cognitive structures significantly distinct from humans, with experts struggling to interpret LLM-derived factors, challenging the assumption of shared cognitive constructs in AI assessment.
